title: Quit India Phase and Bengal War Governance
subtitle: Quit India, wartime measures and provincial politics in Bengal, 1942
summary: In 1942, the Quit India campaign unfolded in Bengal amid wartime restrictions and the prospect of a Japanese advance. Colonial “denial” measures, including restrictions on boats and rice in vulnerable coastal areas, disrupted transport and daily life. After the All-India Congress Committee adopted the Quit India resolution on 8 August, mass arrests and repression followed; local political networks and revolutionary groups shaped the campaign in Bengal. Historians differ over the relative weight of wartime disruption, rumour and organized activism.
heroTagline: Quit India and wartime governance in Bengal, 1942
whyItMatters: The Bengal chapter links the all-India Quit India call to provincial conditions: military precautions, disruption of everyday life and distinctive rural political mobilization. Anwesha Roy emphasizes the interaction of wartime anxieties, rumours and revolutionary activism; other accounts stress denial policies. The evidence supports a layered explanation rather than a single cause.

historicalDebate: Accounts differ over the relative weight of wartime denial measures, popular anxieties and rumour, and organized rural activism in shaping Bengal’s Quit India phase. This chapter presents them as interacting conditions rather than a single cause.
